title: Exercise 1: Typhoon Day WhatsApp Chat
instructions: Complete the following WhatsApp conversation with the correct forms of the verbs in brackets. The first one has been done as an example. (12 marks)
example: Kelly: Jason, have you seen the news? A typhoon is heading our way! If the Observatory e.g. hoists (hoist) Signal No. 8 tomorrow morning, we won't have the Maths test.

rules.form: v(basic) without the third person singular -s when -s is needed
v-ing without the verb to be
Use do/does/did not instead of am/is/are/was/were not, or vice versa
For a main-verb negative, use am/is/are/was/were + not instead of do/does/did not

blanks.explanation: Use 'lowers'. This Type 0 sentence describes what always happens, and the singular subject 'the Observatory' takes an -s verb.
Use 'will have' for the possible result tomorrow. This is Type 1: if + present simple, then will + base verb.
Use 'will you do' to ask about a real possibility tomorrow (Type 1). Put 'will' before 'you' and use the base verb 'do'.
Use ‘go’. Mum is stating a general truth: in this Type 0 conditional, both clauses use the present simple.
Use 'are' for Jason’s usual pattern: Type 0 uses the present simple in the if-clause. 'Supermarkets' is plural, so use 'are'.
Use 'do not finish'. This is a real possibility for tonight, so use the present simple negative in the if-clause: I do not + finish.
Use 'start' in the if-clause for this real possibility. The result is 'you'll be done before dinner', so this is a Type 1 conditional.
Use ‘were’ because Kelly is imagining herself as the Chief Executive. This Type 2 sentence uses ‘if I were’ with ‘I would give’ for the imagined result.
Use 'would want'. Jason is imagining the result of Kelly's made-up plan, so Type 2 uses would + the base verb.
Use 'would feel'. Her cousin imagines having typhoon days, so this Type 2 sentence uses 'would + base verb' for the result, even before the if-clause.
Use 'gets': 'It happens every single time' shows a repeated result, so Type 0 fits here. 'Rainwater' is singular, so add -s to 'get'.
Use 'does not raise'. In this Type 1 sentence about tomorrow, the if-clause uses the present simple, and 'the Observatory' takes 'does'.
